section_summary: This section chiefly documents applications, clearances, and administrative procedures for foreign traders, officials, researchers, and dependents entering or leaving occupied Japan. It includes a proposed seven-day tourist program, Commerce Department applicant lists, individual permit cases, a withdrawn Siamese trade mission, and requests concerning Edward C. Carter’s research visit. Several records concern Moise Moiseeff’s military, re-entry, and exit permits, while later documents address Egyptian trade representation and Victor Kelly Bashi’s renewed clearance.

subfiles.title: Commerce list action sheet for Victor C. Moecke
subfiles.about: Records action on Victor C. Moecke’s proposed sixty-day business visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lists Moecke’s firm, proposed entry period, identification requirements, and responsibility for expenses.

subfiles.title: Ruxton Textile Mills application for Victor C. Moecke
subfiles.about: Requests Japanese entry for Victor C. Moecke to renew contracts and arrange future purchases.
subfiles.summary: The application identifies Moecke, his company and Singapore contact, proposed business, transportation, arrival, itinerary, and length of stay.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing Victor C. Moecke’s entry
subfiles.about: Authorizes Moecke to enter Japan during July for sixty days.
subfiles.summary: Orders notification of Moecke’s clearance and passport-photograph and SCAP documentation requirements.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch on proposed package tourism
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed prepaid package-tour system for foreign tourists in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The despatch outlines carrier notification, a $175 prepaid fare, Japan Travel Bureau services, the planned seven-day itinerary, and tourism’s value as an invisible export.

subfiles.title: Overall procedure and seven-day package tour in Japan
subfiles.about: Sets procedures, conditions, liability rules, prices, and itinerary for organized tours of Japan.
subfiles.summary: The plan assigns publicity, booking, remittance, hotel, railway, automobile, and guiding responsibilities among the carriers and Japan Travel Bureau. A $175 prepaid fare covers transportation, lodging, meals, guides, transfers, and sightseeing. The seven-day itinerary visits Tokyo, Nikkō, Kamakura, Hakone, Atami, Kyoto, and Nara.

subfiles.title: Memorandum concerning Didiricaw Elliott
subfiles.about: Records a request to clear a Dutch woman accompanying her husband’s business party to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Didiricaw Elliott could enter Japan with the Standard Vacuum Oil party for an indefinite stay.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing Didiricaw Elliott’s entry
subfiles.about: Authorizes Didiricaw Elliott to enter Japan with her husband and party.
subfiles.summary: The embassy is instructed to furnish clearance documentation and advise Elliott of photographic requirements.

subfiles.title: London airgram on Pakistani applications
subfiles.about: Reports British efforts to clarify Japanese entry rules for Pakistani applicants.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office will write again to Karachi after notifying its high commissioners in Karachi and New Delhi.

subfiles.title: Army notice concerning Emil Ott
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Reports action on Emil Ott’s request to travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Army communicates its decision concerning British trader Emil Ott’s Japanese entry request.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing Emil Ott’s entry
subfiles.about: Authorizes British national Emil Ott to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The consulate is directed to document Ott’s clearance and require two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Return of Moise Moiseeff’s superseded military permit
subfiles.about: Returns Moiseeff’s unused original permit after a later permit was issued.
subfiles.summary: Moiseeff could not use the first permit because his U.S. re-entry permit arrived late.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department list of approved Japan and Korea travelers
subfiles.about: Forwards applicants approved by Commerce, subject to SCAP’s final decision.
subfiles.summary: The attached lists identify American, Japanese, Dutch, and other business travelers, their firms, proposed dates and transportation, and whether they sought entry to Japan, Korea, or both.

subfiles.title: Moise Moiseeff’s request for a renewed Japanese permit
subfiles.about: Requests rapid issuance of a new Japanese entry permit after immigration delays prevented use of the first.
subfiles.summary: Moiseeff explains that his U.S. re-entry permit had not arrived, returns the expiring Army permit, and seeks replacement documents before sailing from San Francisco aboard President Cleveland.

subfiles.title: Moiseeff letter to the Commissioner of Immigration and Naturalization
subfiles.about: Asks that his delayed U.S. re-entry permit be issued immediately.
subfiles.summary: Moiseeff says the delay threatens his other permits and planned departure for Japan.

subfiles.title: Airgram on the Soviet Mission’s members and dependents
subfiles.about: Reports entry and exit-clearance issues and statistics for Soviet Mission personnel and dependents.
subfiles.summary: The airgram enumerates Allied Council members, dependents, families, and pending Soviet entry or exit requests.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to the Argentine Embassy concerning Américo Guerra
subfiles.about: Acknowledges supplemental information and reports delivery of Guerra’s Japanese military permit.
subfiles.summary: After forwarding Argentina’s information to the Army, the Department received Américo Guerra’s permit and delivered it to his agent, Mrs. Gray Trümpy.

subfiles.title: Instruction concerning the Attia family’s arrival in Panama
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Panama
subfiles.about: Reports that Murad Attia’s family received Panamanian visas and U.S. transit certificates.
subfiles.summary: The mission is asked to notify Panama’s Foreign Office that the family probably has arrived.

subfiles.title: Chilean acknowledgment of Yamada Yoshiro’s repatriation
subfiles.about: Thanks the Department for helping repatriate Hiroshi Yamada Yoshiro from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Chile acknowledges his June 4 departure aboard President Wilson and presumed arrival in Chile.

subfiles.title: Submission of Harry Julius Hurwitz’s application
subfiles.about: Forwards a South African-sponsored application for Hurwitz to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Chappell requests SCAP consideration and says a clearance memorandum will suffice if approved.

subfiles.title: Continuation concerning a proposed Siamese Trade Mission
subfiles.about: Describes the proposed Siamese mission and requests SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: The fragment names the secretary and interpreter and explains the mission’s purchasing purpose and proposed one-month stay.

subfiles.title: Commerce-approved applicants for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards another list of business travelers approved by Commerce, subject to SCAP approval.
subfiles.summary: The list records applicants, firms, nationalities, desired entry dates, and modes of travel, including several previously cleared companies.

subfiles.title: Memorandum concerning Bernard Jacob Etzin
subfiles.about: Records Etzin’s Japanese-entry and U.S. re-entry applications and his attorney’s contact information.
subfiles.summary: Etzin was a stateless Orientex representative seeking business entry into Japan.

subfiles.title: Bernard Jacob Etzin alien departure application
subfiles.about: Requests permission to leave the United States for business in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Etzin describes his Kobe birth and residence, Army employment, Orientex assignment, property, references, intended travel, and pending re-entry permit. He expects an absence exceeding one year.

subfiles.title: Request to clear the Siamese Trade Mission
subfiles.about: Submits ten Siamese officials and businesspeople for permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The mission planned to inspect Japanese markets and purchase goods using sterling and other currencies during a one-month visit.

subfiles.title: Notification of Paul Ernst Ehrlich’s clearance
subfiles.to: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP approval of Paul Ernst Ehrlich’s sixty-day entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: The note gives the August 10–September 10 entry window and explains the required passport endorsement under SCAP Circular 5.

subfiles.title: Moiseeff telegram requesting permit action
subfiles.about: Asks whether his Japanese permit was reissued and seeks help obtaining his re-entry permit.
subfiles.summary: Moiseeff cites his planned July 17 departure aboard President Cleveland.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting Moiseeff’s renewed military permit
subfiles.about: Sends Moiseeff’s reissued permit, valid July 8–August 8.
subfiles.summary: The letter notes prior consultation with Immigration and Moiseeff’s planned departure.

subfiles.title: Telephonic waiver for Moise Moiseeff
subfiles.about: Records waiver of Moiseeff’s exit permit for his July 17 sailing.
subfiles.summary: Waives the exit permit because Moiseeff was traveling to Japan under the traders quota.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Moiseeff’s re-entry application
subfiles.about: Records repeated inquiries to Immigration concerning Moiseeff’s missing re-entry-permit file.
subfiles.summary: Miss Desmond reported that officials were trying to locate the application.

subfiles.title: Moise Moiseeff addressed envelope
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Envelope for Moiseeff’s correspondence from San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Addressed to Walter F. Chappell at the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Moiseeff acknowledgment of renewed permit
subfiles.about: Thanks Chappell for the renewed permit and confirms imminent departure.
subfiles.summary: Moiseeff states that all papers are ready and he will sail aboard President Cleveland.

subfiles.title: Siamese request for a trade mission to Japan
subfiles.about: Requests assistance securing SCAP entry permission for a ten-member Siamese Trade Mission.
subfiles.summary: The mission would inspect Japanese markets, negotiate purchases in sterling and other currencies, and remain about one month.

subfiles.title: South African note transmitting Paul Ernst Ehrlich’s application
subfiles.from: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Transmits Ehrlich’s sponsored application for admission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: South Africa requests notification of the application’s outcome.

subfiles.title: Submission of Paul Ernst Ehrlich’s application to the Army
subfiles.about: Forwards Ehrlich’s South African-sponsored entry application for SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: Chappell requests a memorandum of theater clearance if SCAP approves Ehrlich.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Moiseeff of permit and waivers
subfiles.about: Reports receipt of Moiseeff’s permit and action on his re-entry and exit documents.
subfiles.summary: The permit was airmailed, Immigration was urged to act, and exit requirements would be waived.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal of the unofficial Siamese Trade Mission request
subfiles.about: Withdraws the earlier request after SCAP invited an official Siamese mission.
subfiles.summary: The Siamese Government chose to reconsider dispatching its previously proposed unofficial mission.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Siamese mission withdrawal
subfiles.about: Acknowledges withdrawal of the unofficial mission request.
subfiles.summary: The Department reports asking the Army’s Military Permit Section to cancel the application.

subfiles.title: Letter canceling the Siamese mission request
subfiles.about: Asks the Army to cancel the request for ten Siamese nationals.
subfiles.summary: The cancellation followed SCAP’s separate invitation for an official trade mission.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning Jakob Szpiro’s permit
subfiles.about: Records Globex’s inquiry about its representative Jakob Szpiro’s Japanese clearance.
subfiles.summary: Irwin Spiro offered to pay for a cable notifying Szpiro in Shanghai once cleared.

subfiles.title: Globex Trading application for Jakob Szpiro
subfiles.from: Irwin Spiro and Globex Trading Company
subfiles.about: Requests Japanese entry for Jakob Szpiro to conduct import-export business.
subfiles.summary: The application identifies Szpiro as a Polish representative in Shanghai, lists banking references, proposed destinations, and a sixty-day visit.

subfiles.title: Letter to Katrine Greene concerning Edward C. Carter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Greene’s request for Carter’s Japanese visit and encloses the Department’s procedural reply.
subfiles.summary: Greene is referred to the parallel response sent to W. L. Holland.

subfiles.title: Greene request for Edward C. Carter’s visit
subfiles.about: Requests a ten-day Japanese visit for Institute of Pacific Relations executive Edward C. Carter.
subfiles.summary: Carter would confer with Japanese scholars, plan exchanges of research materials, and assess how the Institute could support Japanese international-relations scholarship. Greene asks that authorization reach Shanghai before his proposed August visit.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to W. L. Holland concerning Carter
subfiles.about: Explains the formal consular and SCAP procedure Carter must follow.
subfiles.summary: Carter must apply at an American consulate, which will route the application through Washington to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Duplicate letter to Katrine Greene
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Greene’s Carter request and encloses the reply to Holland.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate administrative copy of the letter concerning Carter’s Japanese clearance.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram on Egypt’s official trade representative
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports clearance of Samir El Khadem as Egypt’s official trade representative in Japan.
subfiles.summary: El Khadem may liaise on trade and execute government contracts but may not represent private interests. Egyptian trader applications should proceed through the United Kingdom liaison mission acting as protecting power.

subfiles.title: Holland request for Edward C. Carter’s visit
subfiles.about: Seeks assistance obtaining permission for Carter to visit Japanese research organizations.
subfiles.summary: Holland describes Carter’s United Nations and Institute assignments and his need to assess the Japan Institute of Pacific Studies. He requests authorization through Shanghai for an early-August Tokyo visit and supplies several official references.

subfiles.title: Copy of Holland request for Edward C. Carter’s visit
subfiles.about: Copies Holland’s request for assistance with Carter’s entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: The copy describes Carter’s Asian research itinerary, proposed consultations in Tokyo, Shanghai routing, and potential references. It emphasizes the importance of first-hand assessment of Japan’s Institute of Pacific Studies.

subfiles.title: Draft procedural reply to Holland
subfiles.about: States that Carter must apply through the nearest American consulate.
subfiles.summary: The application would pass through the Department to SCAP, with any approval cabled to Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Additional copy of letter to Katrine Greene
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Greene’s Carter request and refers her to the Department’s reply to Holland.
subfiles.summary: An additional file copy concerning Edward C. Carter’s proposed visit.

subfiles.title: Final reply to W. L. Holland concerning Carter
subfiles.about: Explains the required route for Carter’s Japanese-entry application.
subfiles.summary: Carter must apply through a consulate; SCAP alone can approve entry, after which Shanghai will receive authorization.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary Paddock telegram
subfiles.about: Fragmentary telegram apparently concerning travel documents or clearance.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR is too incomplete to identify the travelers or requested action reliably.

subfiles.title: Paddock telegram concerning Japanese sisters
subfiles.about: Requests assistance verifying relatives and clearance for two Japanese sisters.
subfiles.summary: The telegram names Nagoa and Anisa, relatives in Japan, and a Tokyo address, while warning that spellings are approximate.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing Victor Kelly Bashi’s entry
subfiles.about: Authorizes Victor Kelly Bashi to enter Japan during September for sixty days.
subfiles.summary: The embassy is instructed to furnish certified clearance text and require two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning Victor Kelly Bashi’s permit
subfiles.about: Records notification of Bashi’s September entry clearance and authorization to cable Bangkok.
subfiles.summary: A. Shebairo confirmed Bashi was in Bangkok and authorized the Department to notify him.

subfiles.title: File note on Victor Kelly Bashi’s requested extension
subfiles.about: Requests extension of Bashi’s expired permit through September 30.
subfiles.summary: Notes Bashi’s firm, nationality, representative status, and prior approval.
